text: Gilbert Ryle distinguished propositional knowledge (knowing-that) from ability knowledge, which he called knowing-___.
explanation: Ryle's distinction separates knowing that a proposition is true from knowing how to carry out an activity, such as how to ride a bicycle. Intellectualists like Stanley and Williamson argue that knowing-how is ultimately a species of knowing-that (propositional knowledge held under a practical mode of presentation), whereas anti-intellectualists hold that it is an irreducible practical ability.
